While I won't be spending any money this weekend – I've cleared my monthly LEGO budget as part of the LEGO Insiders Weekend – a few deals have caught my eye and deserve some time in the spotlight. posts.title: LEGO Architecture New York drops to lowest price ever: 33% off at £87.74 on Amazon
posts.description: LEGO Architecture's huge and stylish New York set is ready to make a statement on display in your home, now at its lowest price ever during Black Friday. The recent range of stylised city skyline models has been making waves in LEGO Architecture, despite only having two entries. Those entries include one for Paris and the larger 21066 New York City – The Big Apple . The 1,365-piece set has been stuck between £100 and the £129.99 RRP since its launch, but a sudden price drop has now surfaced. Amazon has 21066 New York City – The Big Apple in stock for £87.74 instead of £129.99. That's a clean 33% discount on this build. Architecture doesn't see many annual releases any more, but they tend to be larger. This can create an obstacle for collectors, which is where sales come in handy. posts.title: LEGO Ideas meets Boy Meets World with latest 10K fan-designed submission
posts.description: ABC’s classic ’90’s sitcom gets the LEGO Ideas treatment with the latest 10K fan-designed submission to make it into the third review of 2026. There’s just over a month to go before the third LEGO Ideas review of 2026 is due to close, but there’s still time for more 10K fan creations to successfully make it across the finish line. The list of models all currently hoping to become future physical sets has now grown once more, with the addition of JJTheOfficeGuy’s Boy Meets World , a brick-built recreation of the hit ABC sitcom. The 2,538-piece tribute to the ’90’s series features two landmark locations from the show’s seven-season run, with the set being packed with plenty of details, along with a selection of 10 fan-favourite minifigure characters. Designed as three separate dioramas that can be combined to form a cohesive whole, Boy Meets World boasts The Matthews’ Home, Mr. Feeny’s Classroom and The Last Ride, complete with a variety of furniture and even a rollercoaster ride car.
